l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus has disposition brave and innocent (as read by Ak in his eyes)
q: The clear eyes met his own steadfastly, and the Woodsman gave a sigh of relief as he marked their placid depths and read the youth's brave and innocent heart.

s: Claus is a human (of human descent)
q: Place your hand upon my girdle and hold fast while we journey through the air; for now shall we encircle the world and look upon many of the haunts of those men from whom you are descended.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Ak teaches mortality and helpfulness (through instruction about human life)
q: "Everything perishes except the world itself and its keepers," answered Ak. "But while life lasts everything on earth has its use. The wise seek ways to be helpful to the world, for the helpful ones are sure to live again."

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Necile is a nymph (of the Forest)

q: The nymph who cared for you as a mother seems now like a sister to you

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Burzee contains Nymphs

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: humanity is a mortals (in contrast to immortals)
q: "Indeed," said Ak, "the immortals are few; but the mortals are many."

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus is a mortal (unlike the immortals)
q: "Then why, if man must perish, is he born?" demanded the boy.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: humanity is diverse many natures (in character and circumstance)
q: Men of many natures were there, as everywhere

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: humanity is affected by wealth and poverty (from birth onward)
q: The difference in the wealth of the parents determines the lot of the child.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: children experience contentment (especially during childhood)
q: Childhood is the time of man's greatest content," said Ak

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: children are divided by wealth and poverty (into differing living conditions)
q: Some are carefully tended and clothed in silks and dainty linen; others are neglected and covered with rags.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: children are equal in fairness and sweetness (as babes)
q: "Yet all seem equally fair and sweet," said Claus, thoughtfully.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: children are found in city of men (in varied social circumstances)
q: But especially he noted the children--first curiously, then eagerly, then lovingly. Ragged little ones rolled in the dust of the streets, playing with scraps and pebbles. Other children, gaily dressed, were propped upon cushions and fed with sugar-plums.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: journey through the world is led by Ak (with Claus as pupil)

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: journey through the world visits city of men (to observe humanity)
q: Ere long there were spires beneath them, while buildings of many shapes and colors met their downward view. It was a city of men

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: journey through the world observes humanity (in many regions and occupations)
q: They visited many dwellings of men in many parts of the world, watching farmers toil in the fields, warriors dash into cruel fray, and merchants exchange their goods for bits of white and yellow metal.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: girdle (Ak's girdle) makes invisible Claus (while Claus holds fast to it)
q: So long as you hold fast to my girdle you will remain unseen by all mankind, though seeing clearly yourself.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus is reared in Burzee (from infancy)
q: "Why was I reared in the forest, among those who are not of my race?"

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: girdle (Ak's girdle) separates Claus (if Claus releases his grasp)
q: To release your grasp will be to separate yourself forever from me and your home in Burzee.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: wild beasts threaten Claus (when he is abandoned as a baby)
q: how he had been abandoned at the forest's edge and left a prey to wild beasts

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus is rescued by Necile (as an abandoned baby)
q: how he had been abandoned at the forest's edge and left a prey to wild beasts, and how the loving nymph Necile had rescued him and brought him to manhood under the protection of the immortals.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus is raised by Necile (under the protection of the immortals)
q: how the loving nymph Necile had rescued him and brought him to manhood under the protection of the immortals.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus is helpful minded helpfulness (toward humanity's children)
q: a longing seized him to become helpful to his fellows

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus pities children (especially the innocent and helpless)
q: And everywhere the eyes of Claus sought out the children in love and pity

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus is thoughtful deep thought (after the journey)

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus is a human
q: I am of the race of men, and man's lot is my lot.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus has home in Laughing Valley (since leaving the Forest)
q: That was many, many years ago. It has been his home ever since. It is his home now.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Necile is a foster-mother
q: My foster-mother," here he stopped and kissed Necile's white forehead, "I shall love and cherish while life lasts.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Necile adopts Claus (as a forsaken babe)
q: For your tender care of the poor, forsaken babe you adopted, as well as for your loving comradeship during my boyhood, my heart will ever overflow with gratitude.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Necile cares for Claus (during his boyhood)
q: For your tender care of the poor, forsaken babe you adopted, as well as for your loving comradeship during my boyhood, my heart will ever overflow with gratitude.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Master Woodsman has authority over the Forest's protection (his Word is the Law)
q: I, the Master Woodsman of the World, have said it, and my Word is the Law!

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Master Woodsman grants the Forest's protection (to Claus)
q: Therefore, when you go forth into the world of men you shall retain the protection of the Forest, and the powers you now enjoy will remain with you to assist you in your labors.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Master Woodsman guides Claus (mercifully, toward his new home)
q: But Ak, who knew the boy's heart, was merciful and guided his steps.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Nymphs is a forest people (fair, youthful, and innocent)
q: You, who live so sweetly in your forest bowers, ever fair and youthful and innocent, are no fit comrades for a son of humanity.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Nymphs serve Claus (gladly when called upon)
q: In any need you may call upon the Nymphs, the Ryls, the Knooks and the Fairies, and they will serve you gladly.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus is a the adopted child (of the Forest)
q: Having been adopted as the child of the Forest, and the playfellow of the nymphs, you have gained a distinction which forever separates you from your kind.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Burzee contains Laughing Valley (at its eastern edge)
q: Coming through Burzee to its eastern edge Claus reached the Laughing Valley of Hohaho.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Laughing Valley has features rolling green hills (on each side)
q: On each side were rolling green hills, and a brook wandered midway between them to wind afar off beyond the valley.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Laughing Valley contains brook (wandering midway between its hills)
q: On each side were rolling green hills, and a brook wandered midway between them to wind afar off beyond the valley.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: brook is a watercourse (in the Laughing Valley of Hohaho)
q: On each side were rolling green hills, and a brook wandered midway between them to wind afar off beyond the valley.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: humanity has lot brief mortal life (including toil, aging, and death)
q: For I have looked upon man, finding him doomed to live for a brief space upon earth, to toil for the things he needs, to fade into old age, and then to pass away as the leaves in autumn.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: humanity has mission to leave the world better (than it was found)
q: Yet every man has his mission, which is to leave the world better, in some way, than he found it.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: humanity is subject to the doom of humanity (the necessity to worry and work)
q: He went forth bravely to meet his doom--the doom of the race of man--the necessity to worry and work.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus's departure from the Forest ends Claus's life in the Forest (as a sweet, wild life)
q: There was no need to say good by, by for him the sweet, wild life of the Forest was over.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus's departure from the Forest leads to the world of men (to undertake his mission)
q: But I must leave you, to take my part in the endless struggle to which humanity is doomed, and to live my life in my own way.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus is a the playfellow of the nymphs
q: Having been adopted as the child of the Forest, and the playfellow of the nymphs, you have gained a distinction which forever separates you from your kind.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus has mission Santa Claus's mission to bring happiness to children (among the children of mankind)
q: I must devote myself to the care of the children of mankind, and try to make them happy

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus retains the Forest's protection (when he enters the world of men)
q: Therefore, when you go forth into the world of men you shall retain the protection of the Forest, and the powers you now enjoy will remain with you to assist you in your labors.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus receives help from Nymphs (when he calls upon them)
q: In any need you may call upon the Nymphs, the Ryls, the Knooks and the Fairies, and they will serve you gladly.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus receives help from Ryls (when he calls upon them)
q: In any need you may call upon the Nymphs, the Ryls, the Knooks and the Fairies, and they will serve you gladly.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus receives help from Knooks (when he calls upon them)
q: In any need you may call upon the Nymphs, the Ryls, the Knooks and the Fairies, and they will serve you gladly.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus receives help from Fairies (when he calls upon them)
q: In any need you may call upon the Nymphs, the Ryls, the Knooks and the Fairies, and they will serve you gladly.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, YOUTH / 1. Burzee
s: The Forest of Burzee is a vast, ancient forest with closely packed trees, dense foliage, mosses, lichens, and dried leaves. It is described as mighty, grand, and filled with peaceful natural sounds and changing shadows. Nature originally populated Burzee with Fairies, Knooks, Ryls, and Nymphs, who live there as sweet immortals. Civilization has never reached the forest, though it is uncertain whether it ever will.

l: Burzee, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, YOUTH / 1. Burzee
s: The Forest of Burzee is a mighty, grand, and ancient forest whose trees have intertwined roots and branches. It provides a home, refuge, and playground for its inhabitants and remains largely untouched by civilization.

l: inhabitants of Burzee, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, YOUTH / 1. Burzee
s: The inhabitants of Burzee are Fairies, Knooks, Ryls, and Nymphs, who were placed there by Nature. They are sweet immortals who live, revel, and play undisturbed in the forest's depths.

l: Civilization, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, YOUTH / 1. Burzee
s: Civilization has never reached the Forest of Burzee. Whether it will ever reach the forest remains uncertain.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. The Child of the Forest
s: Necile, a wood-nymph of the Forest of Burzee, becomes restless with her uneventful duties and longs for meaningful adventure. Ak tells the nymphs that he found a human infant abandoned near the forest and ordered the lioness Shiegra to protect it and feed it. Defying the Law of the Forest, Necile leaves the forest’s depths, finds the sleeping infant, and carries it away into the forest after it reaches for her.

l: Necile, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. The Child of the Forest
s: Necile is a beautiful wood-nymph related to Queen Zurline who guards trees in the Forest of Burzee. As her duties become easier and less frequent, she grows discontented and longs for adventure. After hearing about a human infant in danger, she breaks the Law of the Forest, finds the child, and carries it into the forest.

l: Burzee, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. The Child of the Forest
s: The Forest of Burzee is a great forest inhabited by wood-nymphs and governed by the Law of the Forest. Its trees have become old and sturdy, and weeds and Gadgols no longer threaten them as they once did.

l: Ak, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. The Child of the Forest
s: Ak is the Master Woodsman of the world and is said to see everything and know more than the sons of men. He sometimes rescues helpless human children from misery, including four children saved from freezing and a newborn infant threatened by a lioness. He orders Shiegra to protect the infant and give it milk until he can attend to other matters.

l: Nymphs, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. The Child of the Forest
s: The wood-nymphs guard forests, minister to young trees, and dress in oak-leaf green. They participate in festivals and dances, listen to Ak’s words of wisdom, and are generally sheltered within the inner parts of the Forest of Burzee by its law.

l: Law of the Forest, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. The Child of the Forest
s: The Law of the Forest restrains wood-nymphs from leaving the forest in search of adventure. Necile knowingly breaks this law when she goes to find the human infant.

l: Shiegra, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. The Child of the Forest
s: Shiegra is a lioness who crouches near the Forest of Burzee, intending to devour the abandoned human infant. Ak commands her to lie beside the infant, feed it her milk, and ensure that no beast or reptile harms it.

l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. The Child of the Forest
s: The human infant is found newborn, naked, helpless, and crying on the grass near the Forest of Burzee. Shiegra quiets its hunger with her milk under Ak’s command, after which the infant sleeps, smiles at Necile, reaches toward her, and is carried into the forest by her.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. The Adoption
s: Ak, the Master Woodsman, discovers that Necile has brought a sleeping human infant into the Forest of Burzee. Necile asks to keep and care for the infant, arguing that Ak can permit her to do so. Ak agrees to the adoption and grants the infant his protection, but declares that no mortal will ever again be adopted by an immortal. Necile rejoices and takes the infant to her bower.

l: Ak, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. The Adoption
s: Ak discovers Necile holding the sleeping infant and recognizes that she has defied his Law. He permits Necile to keep the infant and promises to protect it, while declaring that this is the final time he will relax the Law.

l: Necile, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. The Adoption
s: Necile brings the sleeping infant into the Forest of Burzee and asks Ak to let her keep and care for it. After Ak grants her request, she hurries to her bower to rejoice over her new-found treasure.

l: Nymphs, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. The Adoption
s: The nymphs are surprised and dismayed to see Necile standing with the infant. They hear Ak permit Necile to keep the child, and Queen Zurline encourages Ak to grant the petition.

l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. The Adoption
s: The infant is sleeping, weak, and helpless when Necile presents it to Ak and the nymphs. Ak allows Necile to keep it and gives it his protection.

l: Burzee, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. The Adoption
s: The Forest of Burzee is the place where Necile wants to raise the infant, although the human race has never penetrated it. Necile considers it her home and believes the infant cannot harm it.

l: the Law, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. The Adoption
s: The Law forbids an immortal from adopting a mortal. Ak relaxes the Law to allow Necile to keep the infant, but declares that it will never again be relaxed for this purpose.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. Claus
s: Necile and the forest nymphs care for the human infant, naming him Claus or Neclaus after the Queen suggests the name. Claus grows up in Necile's bower, fed by milk from bell-udders, does, and Shiegra, while Necile teaches him to speak, walk, and play. Ak's decree protects Claus from the beasts, and the Ryls, Knooks, and Fairies visit him and become fond of him. Claus learns their laws and believes the Forest of Burzee is the whole world, unaware that other human beings exist.

l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. Claus
s: Claus is raised by Necile and the forest nymphs in Necile's bower, where he grows big and sturdy. He is gentle, fearless, playful, and loved by the Ryls, Knooks, and Fairies; he learns their laws and believes the forest is the entire world.

l: Necile, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. Claus
s: Necile names the infant Claus, gathers soft moss for his bed, and cares for him in her bower. She teaches him to speak, walk, and play, and loves to call him Claus even after the Queen suggests the name Neclaus.

l: Ak, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. Claus
s: Ak sanctions the nymphs' adoption of the human infant. His decree forbids beasts and reptiles from molesting Claus, allowing him to walk fearlessly through the forest.

l: Nymphs, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. Claus
s: The forest nymphs gather around Claus with curiosity and delight and praise Ak for allowing Necile to keep him. They search for bell-udders to provide him with milk and help care for him as he grows.

l: Burzee, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. Claus
s: The Forest of Burzee is where Claus is raised and where the nymphs, Ryls, Knooks, and Fairies visit him. Claus comes to regard it as the whole world because he does not know that other human beings exist.

l: Claus's adoption by Necile, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. Claus
s: The adoption of Claus by Necile and the forest nymphs is sanctioned by Ak. It attracts the interest of the Ryls, Knooks, and Fairies, whose customs or laws had not prepared them for an immortal community adopting a human child.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. The Master Woodsman
s: Claus grows from infancy to a stalwart youth while living among Necile and the immortals of Burzee. He learns the language and lore of the forest and helps the Ryls and Knooks with their work. When Ak returns to Burzee, he observes Claus closely and decides to take him on a journey through the world. Necile grieves at the separation and clings to Claus as Ak watches them thoughtfully.

l: Burzee, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. The Master Woodsman
s: Burzee remains a vast forest inhabited by nymphs, Ryls, Knooks, and many animals. Claus explores its heart, learns its natural lore, and helps maintain its plants and animals.

l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. The Master Woodsman
s: Claus grows to manhood, becoming a broad-shouldered and stalwart youth. He learns the language of the beasts, the songs of the bees, the poetry of the wood-flowers, and the history of Burzee's owls, while helping the Ryls and Knooks. Ak later asks him to accompany him on a journey through the world.

l: Necile, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. The Master Woodsman
s: Necile raises Claus and comes to love him dearly. She adapts her life to follow him through Burzee and teaches him about the forest and its inhabitants. She weeps when Ak takes Claus away for a time and clings to him as if she cannot bear to let him go.

l: Ak, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. The Master Woodsman
s: Ak returns to Burzee after visiting his many forests throughout the world. He studies Claus's face and is relieved to find his eyes placid and his heart brave and innocent. He calls Claus aside and tells him to accompany him on a journey through the world.

l: Nymphs, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. The Master Woodsman
s: The nymphs remain immortal and unchanging while Claus grows from a child into a youth. They follow Claus through the forest paths, explain Burzee's mysteries and living creatures to him, and protect and favor him along with Queen Zurline.

l: journey through the world, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. The Master Woodsman
s: Ak plans for Claus to accompany him on a journey through the world after Ak has visited his many forests. Claus is pleased by the honor, while Necile is distressed by his departure.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. Claus Discovers Humanity
s: Ak takes Claus on a journey around the world so he can see the many human beings from whom he is descended. Claus learns that humanity is numerous, unequal in wealth and circumstances, and subject to mortality, while the immortals are few. He becomes especially interested in the children and longs to help them, remembering how Necile rescued him as a baby. When Claus returns to the Forest of Burzee, he is thoughtful and no longer as carefree as before.

l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. Claus Discovers Humanity
s: Claus travels with Ak through the air and visits many human settlements while remaining invisible by holding the Master's girdle. He learns that he is descended from humanity and that he was abandoned at the forest's edge before Necile rescued him. After seeing the lives of people and children, he longs to become helpful to his fellows and returns to Burzee grave and thoughtful.

l: Ak, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. Claus Discovers Humanity
s: Ak takes Claus around the world to show him the haunts and lives of human beings. He explains the differences between mortals and immortals, the unequal conditions of children, Claus's babyhood, and the purpose of helpful lives. He returns Claus safely to the Forest of Burzee.

l: Necile, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. Claus Discovers Humanity
s: Necile had rescued Claus when he was abandoned at the edge of the forest and had brought him to manhood under the protection of the immortals. She anxiously awaits his return and sighs when she sees how deeply thoughtful he has become.

l: Burzee, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. Claus Discovers Humanity
s: The Forest of Burzee is Claus's home, where he was reared among the immortals after Necile rescued him. Ak and Claus return there after traveling around the world, and Claus is set down among the circle of nymphs.

l: humanity, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. Claus Discovers Humanity
s: Humanity is numerous and includes people with many different natures, conditions, and occupations. Mortals must struggle and worry for wealth, eventually perish, and are born in both cottages and palaces. Ak teaches that helpful people are sure to live again.

l: children, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. Claus Discovers Humanity
s: Claus observes children living in poverty and wealth, including ragged children playing in dust and richly dressed children fed with sugar-plums. He sees them as equally fair and sweet and believes childhood is the time of greatest content, before the cares of humanity overtake them. Their condition awakens his love, pity, and desire to help.

l: journey through the world, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. Claus Discovers Humanity
s: Ak's journey around the world with Claus begins in a clearing in the Forest of Burzee and carries them through the air to cities and dwellings in many parts of the earth. They observe farmers, warriors, merchants, and children before returning to Burzee. The journey changes Claus from an ever-joyous boy into a grave and thoughtful youth.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
s: Claus tells Queen Zurline and the Forest people that, as a son of humanity, he must leave the Forest and accept the brief, difficult life of mankind. He chooses to devote himself to caring for the children of mankind, hoping to make them happy as Necile made him happy. Ak grants Claus continued protection and the assistance of the Nymphs, Ryls, Knooks, and Fairies. Claus leaves Burzee and chooses the Laughing Valley of Hohaho as his home.

l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
s: Claus recognizes that he belongs to humanity and decides to leave the Forest to live according to mankind's lot. He chooses to devote his life to making children happy, and Ak grants him continued protection and the aid of the Forest people.

l: Necile, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
s: Necile is remembered by Claus as his loving foster-mother and comrade. Claus kisses her and promises to love and cherish her while he lives, while she silently embraces and kisses him tenderly at his departure.

l: Master Woodsman, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
s: Ak confirms that Claus has spoken well and declares that Claus will retain the Forest's protection and his existing powers after entering the world of men. Ak also promises that the Nymphs, Ryls, Knooks, and Fairies will serve Claus when he calls upon them, and he guides Claus's steps after he leaves.

l: Nymphs, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
s: The nymphs listen as Claus explains why he must leave them and proudly promise to give him their sympathy and help. They remain among the Forest people whose aid Ak grants Claus.

l: Burzee, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
s: Burzee remains the Forest that Claus leaves when he begins his life among men. Claus passes through Burzee to reach its eastern edge and the Laughing Valley of Hohaho.

l: Laughing Valley, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
s: The Laughing Valley of Hohaho lies at the eastern edge of Burzee, between green hills with a brook running through it. Its cheerful natural life restores Claus's merriment, and he chooses the valley as his home.

l: humanity, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
s: Humanity is described as living briefly, working for its needs, growing old, and dying, while each person has a mission to leave the world better than they found it. Claus accepts humanity's lot as his own and leaves the Forest to take his part in its struggle.

l: Claus's departure from the Forest, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
s: Claus says farewell to the Forest people by turning away rather than speaking a formal goodbye, because his wild Forest life is over. He then passes through Burzee and goes out toward the world of men.

l: Santa Claus's mission to bring happiness to children, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
s: Claus decides to care for the children of mankind and devote his life to their pleasure. He hopes that Necile's kindness in adopting and caring for him will be remembered through the happiness he brings to thousands of children.

l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
s: Claus settles in the Laughing Valley and begins building a home without harming living trees or flowers. The Knooks build his house, while the Fairies provide household tools, food-preparation items, clothing, blankets, and other comforts. The Spirit of Happiness removes Claus's fears and cares, and the Ryls of the Field Flowers promise to supply his food so he will not need to cultivate the flower-filled ground. Claus therefore begins a peaceful life supported by the immortals.

l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
s: Claus comes to the empty Laughing Valley, builds a house from fallen trees, and chooses not to cut living trees or destroy flowers. He receives help and supplies from the Knooks, Fairies, and Ryls of the Field Flowers, and begins a happy life devoted to doing good.

l: Laughing Valley, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
s: The Laughing Valley is a peaceful, flower-filled place inhabited by grass, a brook, wildflowers, bees, and butterflies. It claims Claus as its tenant, brings him happiness, and becomes his home.

l: Master Woodsman, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
s: The Master Woodsman sends his servant Nelko with a strong, bright ax for Claus. He also sends the Fairies to provide Claus with household supplies and clothing.

l: immortals, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
s: The immortals appear to have directed Claus's steps toward the Laughing Valley after he left Burzee. The Knooks, Fairies, Ryls, and other friendly beings support him there.

l: Forest, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
s: The Forest has taught Claus that living trees are sacred and endowed with feeling. Claus applies this lesson by using only fallen trees for his house.
